## Waffle Charts: Proportions at a Glance {.smaller}

[Cohort summaries]{.eyebrow}

### Part-to-whole as a grid

**Purpose:** Show part-to-whole relationships as a grid of squares — more intuitive than pie charts for proportions.

**When to use:**

- Sample composition (cell types, genotypes)
- Cohort demographics
- Variant classification counts
- Any whole-number percentage summary

**Library:** `PyWaffle` — `pip install pywaffle`

<!-- slide 115 -->
## Waffle Charts — Result {.plot-slide background-color="#f6f4ee"}

[Cohort summaries]{.eyebrow}

### PBMC cell-type composition

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 5

from pywaffle import Waffle

cell_counts = {
    'T cells'    : 38,
    'B cells'    : 22,
    'NK cells'   : 15,
    'Monocytes'  : 14,
    'Other'      : 11,
}

fig = plt.figure(
    FigureClass = Waffle,
    rows        = 10,
    values      = cell_counts,
    colors      = [BRAND, ACCENT_YLW, ACCENT_PURP, RED, GRAY_DARK],
    title       = {'label': 'PBMC Cell-Type Composition', 'fontsize': 11,
                   'fontweight': 'bold'},
    legend      = {'loc': 'lower left', 'bbox_to_anchor': (0, -0.3),
                   'ncol': 3, 'fontsize': 8},
    figsize     = (6, 5),
    block_aspect_ratio = 1,
)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Waffle Chart: Code Walkthrough {.smaller .scrollable}

[Cohort summaries]{.eyebrow}

### Waffle in PyWaffle

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "1-9|11-23|25-30"

from pywaffle import Waffle
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Step 1: Define counts (absolute or relative)
cell_composition = {
    'T cells'    : 38,
    'B cells'    : 22,
    'NK cells'   : 15,
    'Monocytes'  : 14,
    'Other'      : 11,
}

# Step 2: Build the figure
fig = plt.figure(
    FigureClass = Waffle,
    rows        = 10,           # number of rows in the grid
    values      = cell_composition,
    colors      = [COLORS['primary'], '#E8A838', COLORS['quinary'], COLORS['primary'], '#606060'],
    icons       = 'circle',     # or 'person', 'square' (Font Awesome icons)
    icon_size   = 12,
    title       = {'label' : 'PBMC Cell-Type Composition',
                   'fontsize': 12, 'fontweight': 'bold'},
    legend      = {'loc': 'lower left', 'bbox_to_anchor': (0, -0.28),
                   'ncol': 3, 'fontsize': 9,
                   'frameon': False},
    figsize     = (8, 5),
)

# Step 3: Save / show
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('waffle_pbmc.pdf', bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()
```

<!-- slide 118 -->
## Waterfall Plots: Mutation Landscapes {.smaller}

[Cohort summaries]{.eyebrow}

### Mutation burden as ranked bars

**Purpose:** Display somatic mutation burden across a patient cohort — a staple of cancer genomics papers.

**What the plot shows:**

- Each bar = one patient, height = tumor mutation burden (TMB)
- Bars sorted by TMB (descending)
- Color can encode cancer subtype, treatment response, or driver mutation
- Often paired with an **OncoPrint** (mutation matrix below)

<!-- slide 119 -->
## Waterfall Plot — Result {.plot-slide background-color="#f6f4ee"}

[Cohort summaries]{.eyebrow}

### TMB ranked, coloured by subtype

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5

np.random.seed(42)
n_patients = 60
tmb = np.sort(np.random.lognormal(3, 1.2, n_patients))[::-1]
subtypes = np.random.choice(['Luminal A','Luminal B','HER2+','TNBC'], n_patients)
color_map_st = {'Luminal A': BRAND, 'Luminal B': ACCENT_YLW,
                'HER2+': ACCENT_PURP, 'TNBC': RED}
colors = [color_map_st[s] for s in subtypes]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5))
ax.bar(range(n_patients), tmb, color=colors, width=1.0, edgecolor='none')
ax.set_xlabel('Patient (sorted by TMB)', fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel('Tumor Mutation Burden\n(mutations / Mb)', fontsize=10)
ax.set_title('Waterfall Plot: Mutation Burden', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)
ax.set_xticks([])

from matplotlib.patches import Patch
legend_elements = [Patch(facecolor=c, label=l)
                   for l, c in color_map_st.items()]
ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, fontsize=8, frameon=False,
          loc='upper right')
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

<!-- slide 121 -->
## Waterfall Plot: Code {.smaller .scrollable}

[Cohort summaries]{.eyebrow}

### From TMB table to ranked bars

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "1-11|13-23|25-35"

# Step 1: Simulate TMB data
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Patch

np.random.seed(42)
n = 80
patients = pd.DataFrame({
    'patient'  : [f'P{i:03d}' for i in range(n)],
    'TMB'      : np.random.lognormal(3, 1.2, n),
    'subtype'  : np.random.choice(['Luminal A','Luminal B','HER2+','TNBC'], n),
    'response' : np.random.choice(['CR','PR','SD','PD'], n,
                                  p=[0.15, 0.35, 0.30, 0.20]),
})

# Step 2: Sort and assign colors
patients = patients.sort_values('TMB', ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
color_map = {'Luminal A':COLORS['primary'],'Luminal B':'#E8A838',
             'HER2+':COLORS['quinary'],'TNBC':COLORS['primary']}
colors = patients['subtype'].map(color_map)

# Step 3: Plot
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 5))
ax.bar(range(n), patients['TMB'], color=colors, width=1.0, edgecolor='none')
ax.set_yscale('log')   # log scale common for TMB
ax.set_xlabel('Patient (sorted by TMB)', fontsize=12, labelpad=8)
ax.set_ylabel('Tumor Mutation Burden (log scale)', fontsize=12, labelpad=8)
ax.set_title('Somatic Mutation Landscape', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold')
ax.spines[['top','right']].set_visible(False)
ax.set_xticks([])
legend_elements = [Patch(facecolor=c, label=l) for l, c in color_map.items()]
ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, frameon=False, loc='upper right')
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

## Exercise: Waffle & Waterfall {.smaller .scrollable}

[Cohort summaries]{.eyebrow}

### Hands-on practice

::: {.exercise}
**Coding Exercise — Waffle & Waterfall**

Task A: visualize cohort cell-type proportions as a waffle chart. Task B: build a waterfall mutation landscape sorted by SNV count, colored by cancer type, with MSI-H patients flagged.

::: {.sandbox}
```{python}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

np.random.seed(2026)

# Dataset 1: Cohort cell-type composition
cohort = {
    'CD4+ T cells' : 312,
    'CD8+ T cells' : 198,
    'B cells'      : 145,
    'NK cells'     : 87,
    'Macrophages'  : 132,
    'Dendritic'    : 64,
    'Other'        : 62,
}

# Dataset 2: Somatic mutations in 100 cancer patients
n = 100
mutations = pd.DataFrame({
    'patient'   : [f'P{i:03d}' for i in range(n)],
    'SNV_count' : np.random.lognormal(4.5, 1.0, n).astype(int),
    'cancer'    : np.random.choice(
        ['BRCA','LUAD','COAD','PRAD'], n, p=[0.3, 0.3, 0.2, 0.2]),
    'MSI'       : np.random.choice(['MSI-H','MSS'], n, p=[0.15, 0.85]),
})

# Your tasks:
# Task A – Waffle chart
#   1. Create a waffle chart of cohort cell-type composition
#   2. Use Font Awesome icons (icons='circle')

# Task B – Waterfall plot
#   1. Sort patients by SNV_count descending
#   2. Color bars by cancer type
#   3. Add a horizontal line at the MSI-H / MSS boundary
#   4. Mark MSI-H patients with a star marker on top of their bar

# Bonus: Combine both plots into one figure with subplots
```
:::

<details>
<summary>Show solution</summary>

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true

import numpy as np, pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pywaffle import Waffle

np.random.seed(42)
cell_types = {'T cells': 35, 'B cells': 20, 'NK cells': 15,
              'Monocytes': 18, 'Dendritic': 12}
cancer_types = ['LUAD','BRCA','COAD','PRAD','SKCM']
n_patients = 100
mut_data = pd.DataFrame({
    'patient'    : [f'P{i:03d}' for i in range(n_patients)],
    'SNV_count'  : np.random.negative_binomial(5, 0.05, n_patients),
    'cancer_type': np.random.choice(cancer_types, n_patients),
    'MSI'        : np.random.choice(['MSI-H','MSS'], n_patients, p=[0.15, 0.85]),
})

cancer_pal = {ct: c for ct, c in zip(cancer_types,
    [COLORS['primary'], COLORS['secondary'], COLORS['tertiary'],
     COLORS['quaternary'], COLORS['quinary']])}

# Task A — Waffle chart
cell_pal_list = [COLORS['primary'], COLORS['secondary'], COLORS['tertiary'],
                 COLORS['quaternary'], COLORS['quinary']]
fig_waffle = plt.figure(
    FigureClass=Waffle, rows=10,
    values=cell_types,
    colors=cell_pal_list,
    legend={'loc': 'lower left', 'bbox_to_anchor': (0, -0.4),
            'ncol': 3, 'frameon': False, 'fontsize': 9},
    figsize=(8, 5),
    facecolor="white",
)
fig_waffle.suptitle('COHORT CELL-TYPE COMPOSITION', fontweight='bold')
plt.show()

# Task B — Waterfall plot
msi_boundary = mut_data['SNV_count'].quantile(0.85)
df_sorted = mut_data.sort_values('SNV_count', ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)

fig2, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 5), facecolor="white")
ax.set_facecolor("white")

bars = ax.bar(range(n_patients),
              df_sorted['SNV_count'],
              color=[cancer_pal[c] for c in df_sorted['cancer_type']],
              width=1.0, linewidth=0)
ax.axhline(msi_boundary, color=COLORS['zero_line'], lw=1.2,
           ls='--', label=f'MSI-H boundary ({msi_boundary:.0f} SNVs)')

msi_mask = df_sorted['MSI'] == 'MSI-H'
ax.scatter(df_sorted.index[msi_mask],
           df_sorted.loc[msi_mask, 'SNV_count'] + 2,
           marker='*', color=COLORS['risk'], s=60, zorder=5, label='MSI-H')

from matplotlib.patches import Patch
legend_els = [Patch(color=v, label=k) for k, v in cancer_pal.items()]
legend_els += [plt.Line2D([0],[0], marker='*', color=COLORS['risk'],
                          ls='none', ms=8, label='MSI-H')]
ax.legend(handles=legend_els, frameon=False, ncol=3, fontsize=9)
ax.set_title('SOMATIC MUTATION LANDSCAPE', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Patients (sorted by SNV count)')
ax.set_ylabel('SNV count')
ax.text(0.01, -0.15, '★ = MSI-H patients. Dashed line = MSI-H/MSS boundary.',
        transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=8.5, style='italic', color=COLORS['text_light'])
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
